children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital/residential accommodation for 15 weeks (>12) and claimant is not regularly spending money on child
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're enquiring about?**

- **Under 16 years old** - Children under 16 generally qualify automatically
- **16 to 19 years old** - There are additional checks needed (they need to be in approved education or training)
- **20 years old or over** - Unfortunately, there wouldn't be eligibility for this child

Please let me know the age of the child (or if you have multiple children, their ages), and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old, so still quite young.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're enquiring about **Alex, who is 8 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check the next eligibility requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is a standard check - most children under 16 wouldn't be working full-time anyway, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 8! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's exactly what I'd expect for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check the next requirement:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, I'm checking if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit in his own right

For an 8-year-old in primary school, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 8 and in primary school, I'm assuming the answer is no. But I need to confirm:
- Is he in any kind of apprenticeship at all?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 years old and in primary school. He's nowhere near old enough for an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency status. This is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Do you (the claimant) meet UK residency requirements?**

There are several paths that can qualify you. Let me ask you about your situation:

1. **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the most straightforward path for most people)

OR are you in one of these situations:

2. Do you have **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme?
3. Do you have **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme? (If so, there are specific conditions depending on your circumstances - e.g., working, seeking work, studying, or family member of an EEA/Swiss national)
4. Are you a **Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries?

What's your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Leeds with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward. You meet the residency requirements. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility can be established in several ways. Since you've already mentioned you live in Leeds with Alex, I'm assuming you live with him. Can you confirm:

- **Do you live with Alex?** (You live in the same household)

OR are you in one of these other situations:

- **Are you contributing to Alex's upkeep?** (This could include paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents - at least the equivalent amount to Child Benefit)
- **Are you paying maintenance towards Alex** under a court order or agreement?

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me in Leeds. We live together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect - you clearly meet the responsibility requirement since you live together. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important point:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied to claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other relative) claiming for him?

Please let me know if there are any other claimants involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if any special circumstances apply regarding where Alex lives:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

- **Normally at home with you** (no special circumstances)
- **In hospital** (there are time limits that might apply)
- **In local authority care** (there are specific rules for this)
- **Fostered** (either by you or elsewhere)

What's Alex's current living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - it's been a few months. He's been getting treatment there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's a challenging situation. Since Alex has been in hospital for a few months, I need to check the specific rules around this.

Let me move forward with the hospital duration check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. The hospital duration is important for eligibility. Let me get more specific information:

**How long has Alex been in hospital continuously, or has he had multiple stays?**

Here's what I need to understand:
- **How many weeks or months has Alex been in hospital** this time?
- **Has Alex been to hospital before and returned home** within the last few months? (If so, I need to know about those stays too, especially if gaps between stays were less than 28 days)

The key rule is that Child Benefit generally continues for up to 12 weeks (cumulative). If there are multiple stays with less than 28 days between them, they all count together towards that 12-week limit.

Can you give me the details of Alex's hospital stay(s)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now, continuously. It's been quite a long stretch.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that's a difficult situation. Since Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks continuously, which exceeds the 12-week limit, this affects his eligibility. However, there's still one more important check I need to make.

Let me continue to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - there's an important exception to the 12-week rule:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?**

This could include things like:
- Visiting expenses (travel, accommodation if staying overnight)
- Bringing him items (clothes, toiletries, books, snacks, etc.)
- Other costs related to his care or comfort while hospitalized

If you're regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay, you may still be eligible for Child Benefit despite exceeding the 12-week period.

Are you regularly spending money on him while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, unfortunately I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's been in there. It's been really difficult financially.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear about your difficult financial situation. Unfortunately, based on the eligibility rules, this means Alex would not qualify for Child Benefit at this time.

Let me continue to verify the final details before I give you the complete outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I've now completed the assessment. Let me provide you with the outcome:

---

## **Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment - INELIGIBLE**

**Child:** Alex (8 years old)

### **Result: INELIGIBLE**

### **Reason:**
Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week limit for Child Benefit eligibility. The rule states that Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks while a child is in hospital or residential accommodation. After this period, eligibility ends unless you are regularly spending money on the child's needs during their hospital stay.

Since you've indicated you haven't been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's been hospitalized, the exception to this rule doesn't apply.

### **Important Information:**

- **The 12-week rule:** Child Benefit generally stops after 12 weeks in hospital/residential care
- **The exception:** If you were regularly spending money on Alex (travel, visits, clothes, toiletries, etc.), you could remain eligible
- **If Alex returns home:** Once he leaves the hospital and returns home, you can reapply for Child Benefit
- **Cumulative counting:** If Alex had been hospitalized before with gaps of less than 28 days, those stays would have counted towards the 12-week limit

### **Next Steps:**

1. **Contact HMRC** to discuss your specific circumstances - there may be exceptions or additional support available
2. **When Alex returns home** from hospital, you can reapply for Child Benefit
3. **Financial support:** If you're struggling financially, you may be eligible for other forms of support. Consider contacting:
   - Your local Citizens Advice Bureau
   - Turn2us (benefits calculator)
   - Your local authority for support services

I'm sorry this news wasn't more positive, especially given your difficult circumstances. However, the situation may change once Alex is discharged from hospital.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So once Alex comes home from the hospital, I can apply again for Child Benefit then?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, exactly! That's correct. Once Alex is discharged from the hospital and returns home to live with you, you would be able to apply for Child Benefit again.

Here's what will happen:

**When Alex comes home:**
- You can submit a new Child Benefit application to HMRC
- At that point, he would no longer be in hospital, so the 12-week hospital rule wouldn't apply
- Based on everything else we've checked today (his age, your residency in the UK, living together, no other claimants, etc.), you should be eligible

**A few things to keep in mind:**
- Make sure to apply as soon as Alex comes home - don't delay the application
- You can apply online through the UK government's Child Benefit portal or by post
- Keep any discharge paperwork from the hospital, as it may be useful for your application
- If you need support with the application process, Citizens Advice or HMRC's helpline can assist you

**In the meantime:**
- If you're facing financial hardship while Alex is in hospital, please do look into other support you might be eligible for (Universal Credit, Council Tax Support, etc.). Your local Citizens Advice Bureau can help you explore these options.

I hope Alex makes a good recovery and can come home soon. Once he does, don't hesitate to apply for Child Benefit - you should be eligible at that point.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about the assessment or the application process?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's really helpful. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly. I'll make sure to apply as soon as Alex comes home. I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify everything for you. You've handled this conversation really well, and you now have a clear picture of what to expect.

Just to recap the key point: **once Alex comes home from hospital, you'll be eligible for Child Benefit**, so make sure to apply promptly at that time.

In the meantime, take care of yourself and I hope Alex makes a speedy recovery. If you have any other questions in the future about Child Benefit or need help with the application process when he comes home, don't hesitate to reach out.

Wishing you and Alex all the best. 💙

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much, that's very kind of you. Take care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! Take care, and all the best to you and Alex. 💙

---

Now let me formally record the outcome of this assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: The assessment has been completed and recorded. I wish you and Alex all the best, and I look forward to helping you with a new application once Alex comes home from hospital.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets most eligibility criteria: he is under 16, not working full-time, not receiving benefits in his own right, not in a disqualifying apprenticeship, his parent is normally resident in the UK (Leeds), his parent lives with him and is responsible for him, and there are no other claimants. However, Alex has been continuously in hospital for 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week cumulative limit for Child Benefit eligibility while in hospital or residential accommodation. Additionally, the parent is not regularly spending money on Alex's needs during the hospital stay, which would be the exception to this 12-week rule. Therefore, Alex is currently ineligible. This situation would change once Alex is discharged from hospital and returns home.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is seeking Child Benefit for their 8-year-old son Alex, whom they live with in Leeds and are solely responsible for. While all other eligibility criteria are met (age, residency, responsibility, no other claimants, and child's work/benefit status), Alex's current ineligibility is due to exceeding the 12-week hospital stay limit. Child Benefit continues for up to 12 weeks in hospital/residential accommodation, but Alex has been hospitalized for 15 weeks. The exception to this rule would apply if the parent were regularly spending money on Alex's needs, but this is not the case due to financial hardship. Once Alex is discharged and returns home, the claimant will be eligible to apply for Child Benefit again."
